title: SSE drop + backpressure repro timeline
content:
Goal: capture a small, repeatable repro for intermittent SSE chunk drops/concatenation when the client is slow (backpressure) and requests are multiplexed.

Symptoms observed:
- Client sometimes receives merged event lines: two separate 'data:' blocks arrive concatenated on the same packet (e.g. 'data: A
data: B
') but delivered as 'data: A
data: B' without trailing newline/flush causing EventSource to treat as one event or drop second.
- Other times the client sees a gap (missing event) when many concurrent streams are open and consumer is artificially slow.
- Happens more frequently when: proxies (envoy/nginx) in front, TLS, and when the server writes small chunks (< 256 bytes) with pauses between writes.

Hypotheses:
1) Proxy buffering + TCP coalescing: Nginx/Envoy is buffering small writes and emitting them together when fronted by TLS, leading to incorrect SSE framing if trailing newlines get lost in transit.
2) Server-side write batching + Node/Golang flush semantics: net/http may buffer until a threshold or until Flush() is called; some code paths didn't call Flush() after last line, so connection stayed open and next event was appended.
3) Kernel-level TCP_CORK/TCP_NODELAY interactions: small writes get grouped into a single packet. If server uses zero-length writes or doesn't terminate lines consistently, client parsers may mis-handle.
4) Client reads by bytes instead of line-oriented, and a slow consumer can cause partial reads that reassemble incorrectly if newline handling is brittle.

Repro plan (local, minimal components):
- Start a tiny SSE server that emits periodic small "data:" events with deliberate delays between writes.
- Put Envoy/nginx configured as reverse proxy (default buffering ON) between server and client and reproduce.
- Vary consumer speed (fast, medium, slow) to trigger backpressure.
- Try with/without TLS.

Commands used so far (server / client / proxy):

1) Minimal Go SSE server (run locally)
# file: sse_server.go (quick run):
// go run sse_server.go

2) curl client (basic)
# use -N to disable buffering in curl
curl -v -N http://localhost:8080/stream

3) httpie streaming test
http --stream GET http://localhost:8080/stream

4) Python raw read (simulates slow consumer)
python3 - <<'PY'
import requests, time
r = requests.get('http://localhost:8080/stream', stream=True)
for line in r.iter_lines(chunk_size=1):
    if line:
        print('RX:', line.decode())
    time.sleep(0.35)  # slow consumer
PY

5) socat client to force packet-level timing (handy to simulate jitter):
# connect and show raw bytes
socat - TCP4:localhost:8080,crnl

6) netcat + hexdump (inspect exact bytes):
echo -e "GET /stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n" | nc localhost 8080 | hexdump -C | sed -n '1,160p'

7) Nginx (simple reverse proxy) config tweaks tested:
- proxy_buffering off;
- proxy_http_version 1.1;
- chunked_transfer_encoding off;
- add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;

8) Envoy bootstrap flags tested:
- stream_idle_timeout and use_remote_address toggles;
- cluster->http2_protocol_options for h2 vs h1;

Observed logs / snippets (server stdout & client hexdump):
- Server wrote:
"data: A

" then after 40ms "data: B

".
- Client hexdump at the TCP level showed a single packet containing: "data: A

data: B

" (as expected). But the EventSource client ended up firing one event with payload "A
data: B" (missing separation) in one browser repro (likely because the browser buffered until double newline?).
- In a different run, server wrote 'data: 1

' then later 'data: 2

', but client observed only '1' then a gap (2 never appeared).
- When I set proxy_buffering off and added 'X-Accel-Buffering: no', frequency dropped but didn't vanish under high concurrency.

Things tried that changed behavior:
- Adding explicit res.Flush() after each write (Go) reduced incidence by ~= 70%.
- Adding a small sleep (5ms) after Flush() sometimes made it worse (coalescing still happened).
- Forcing Connection: keep-alive vs close had minor effects.
- Setting TCP_NODELAY on server socket eliminated certain coalescing cases locally, but not when Envoy in front.
- Switching to TLS increased incidence (likely because of TLS record layering and different flush semantics).

Next repro commands to run (concrete):
1) Local Go server (blocking writes + flush):
# paste into sse_server.go and run
# Run server:
go run sse_server.go &

2) Local client that simulates slow consumer and prints exact byte boundaries:
# node: stream-reader.js (simple TCP client)
node stream-reader.js localhost 8080 slow

3) Pipeline with nginx (config snippet below)
# nginx.conf server block
location /stream {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080/stream;
    proxy_set_header Connection "";  # avoid adding close
    proxy_buffering off;
    proxy_cache off;
    chunked_transfer_encoding off;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
}

4) Try with curl in very slow mode (read 200ms between bytes):
# Use --limit-rate to slow download
curl -N --limit-rate 5B http://localhost:8080/stream

5) Capture packets with tcpdump while running Python slow consumer:
sudo tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -w sse-test.pcap port 8080 &
py-run && sudo pkill tcpdump
# analyze with Wireshark to see TLS/TCP record boundaries

Debug checklist (what to verify when reproducing):
- Are the SSE delimiters (double newline) present in wire trace? If double newline present but client grouped, issue is client parsing. If delimiters missing, server/proxy coalesced.
- Does enabling/disabling proxy_buffering change behavior? (it should)
- Does adding explicit flushes + TCP_NODELAY on server socket eliminate the problem without proxy? If yes, root cause likely server buffering/stack.
- Under TLS, do we see TLS records that combine multiple writes? If so, consider explicit TLS record flush via small write or library option.

Quick notes / heuristics discovered:
- Browsers are picky: Chrome's EventSource tends to buffer until it sees full event (two newlines). If a trailing newline is missing due to partial write, the event is incomplete and might be concatenated with next data.
- Nginx has multiple buffering layers: proxy_buffering plus fastcgi buffers. 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' helps but not guaranteed with HTTP/2 upgrade.
- Envoy may fuse small writes into a single downstream flush for efficiency. There's an Envoy flag to tune streaming flush threshold.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Reproduce with HTTP/2 (server nghttp2) vs HTTP/1.1 to see how framing differs for SSE.
- Try a pure TLS termination (nginx) vs plain TLS in server to isolate where coalescing happens.
- Add a test harness that asserts per-event arrival times and counts (simple harness in Go that spawns N clients with slow readers).

Immediate action items:
- (Priya) finish small Go repro server + harness by 2025-11-06 and link as runnable command.
- (Evan) test with Envoy config adjustments, capture pcap, post results in linked Slack thread.
- (María) run browser-based test with local proxy disabled to confirm browser parsing vs network issue.

Scratchpad: small Go server (copy for my notes)
--
package main
import (
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "time"
)
func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
    w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
    flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
    if !ok { fmt.Println("no flush") }
    for i:=0;i<100;i++ {
        fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %d\\n\\n", i)
        flusher.Flush()
        time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
    }
}
func main(){
    http.HandleFunc("/stream", handler)
    http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil)
}
--

Keep logging exact bytes (hexdump) and attach pcap to ticket INF-987.

If anyone else hits this, try to reproduce with pure TCP client reading bytes and check for missing '\n\n' sequences — that's the minimal indicator of coalescing/truncation.

End of scratchpad.
